_provenance.built_by: independent oracle (metrics_oracle.py + rules_build_fixtures.py), written from the interface spec and the literature, never from engine/uplift; copied into the repo by the oracle-conformance track on 2026-09-23
_provenance.trimmed: curve_every_k stored as parallel arrays indexed by k (fraction = k/n); the 101-point interpolated grid, library cross-checks and the oracle-RNG bootstrap draws are dropped

meta.source: metrics_oracle.py (independent, loop-based) built from UPLIFT_INTERFACES.md Stage A
meta.notes: See metrics_NOTES.md. None = undefined (JSON null). curve_every_k has fraction=k/n. qini_points_101_interpolated samples the per-k curve at i/100 by linear interpolation; compare implementation QiniPoints by evaluating the oracle curve at the point's own fraction.

cases.name: basic8_distinct_sorted
cases.why: hand-computed in metrics_NOTES.md; zero ATE; top-1 has no control -> uplift@0.1 None; n<10 -> deciles 9,10 empty

cases.name: ties6_stable_order
cases.why: tie blocks {0,1,2} and {3,4}; stable sort on -pred keeps input order; hand-computed AUUC = -1/54, qini_coefficient = 0

cases.name: treated_only_first4
cases.why: first 4 ranked rows are treated (no control): Qini scaled term 0, U(k)=0 for k<=4, uplift@0.1/0.2/0.3 None

cases.name: control_only_first3_unsorted
cases.why: input NOT sorted; first 3 ranked rows are control (no treated): U(k)=0 there but Qini(k) = 0 - Y_c*0/N_c = 0

cases.name: all_treated_top_decile_n20
cases.why: decile 1 (2 rows) all treated -> control_rate/observed_uplift None; uplift@0.1 (2 rows) None; uplift@0.2 defined

cases.name: perfect_ranking_n12
cases.why: treated responders first, control responders last (distinct scores): AUUC and qini_coefficient > 0

cases.name: reversed_ranking_n12
cases.why: same rows, pred negated: AUUC and qini_coefficient < 0

cases.name: constant_pred_n7
cases.why: all predictions equal: ranking = input order (stable); sklift collapses the curve to (0,0)-(n,Qini(n)) so its area differs

cases.name: n13_uneven_deciles_negative_ate
cases.why: n=13 -> array_split sizes 2,2,2,1,1,1,1,1,1,1; negative ATE (sleeping-dog-like data); ceil(0.1*13)=2, ceil(0.2*13)=3, ceil(0.3*13)=4

cases.name: medium_seed11_n250
cases.why: random: balanced arms, continuous preds; generator: see metrics_build_fixtures.medium_cases

cases.name: medium_seed22_n400
cases.why: random: 30% treated, continuous preds; generator: see metrics_build_fixtures.medium_cases

cases.name: medium_seed33_n300
cases.why: random: preds rounded to 2 decimals -> many ties; generator: see metrics_build_fixtures.medium_cases

meta.why: The three medium bootstrap fixtures cannot tell a whole-table bootstrap from a within-arm one (checked: whole-table intervals land within 4 sd of the within-arm reference on all 3 cases x 3 seeds), and none of them ever produces an undefined replicate. These two cases can.

cases.name: undefined_replicate_gives_null_interval_n20
cases.note: Top 2 rows are one treated + one control, so the point value is defined. Within-arm resampling puts two rows of the same arm on top in a large share of replicates, so any 200-resample bootstrap has an undefined replicate. ConfidenceValue contract: interval null, never NaN, never silently dropped.

cases.name: arm_sizes_kept_tiny_control_n40
cases.note: 2 control rows of 40. Within-arm resampling always keeps 2 control rows, so every replicate is defined and the ATE / uplift@1.0 / AUUC intervals are non-null. A whole-table bootstrap loses the control arm in 12.9% of replicates, so its interval is null (or NaN, or it crashes).
